data.title: Hyperliquid traders bet on Anthropic after platform ends up on Hong Kong’s warning list
data.description:
Hong Kong has just put Hyperliquid [HYPE] on its watchlist. And yet, traders don’t seem to be bothered.

In fact, on Hyperliquid itself, the action is only heating up now.

Hong Kong’s SFC flags Hyperliquid for operating without a license

On Wednesday, Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added Hyperliquid to its Alert List. The problem cited was that they don’t hold a licence to operate in the city.

The regulator’s entry covers two names; Hyperliquid and Hyperliquid Hong Kong. It also shared the exchange’s trading website. It is believed that the platform may be serving Hong Kong users, presenting itself as a local operator, or pitching its services to people in the city.

With this addition, the SFC’s list of suspicious crypto trading platforms has grown to 69 names now. At the time of writing, Hyperliquid hadn’t commented on the development.

Back in June, Singapore’s central bank placed Hyperliquid on its Investor Alert List which flags firms people might wrongly assume are regulated there. At the time, Hyperliquid’s response was simple — it never said it had a Singapore licence.

Now, there are two Asian financial hubs keeping an eye on the exchange.

Anthropic perps on Hyperliquid make big noise

While Hong Kong was flagging Hyperliquid, traders on the platform were busy betting on Anthropic.

On 18th November, the number of traders holding long positions on Anthropic perps hit a record 5,567.

A week ago, that figure was 2,926; nearly doubling in seven days. There were 1,996 short holders, with the same hinting at 2.8 longs for every short.

Most of that action was on Trade[XYZ]’s ANT market. According to Token Terminal, this alone accounted for 4,190 long holders,.

One caveat, though. These numbers count traders, not the size of their bets. And since the data adds up three markets, anyone trading on two of them gets counted twice.

How’s HYPE handling all this?

Not great, but not terrible either.

The altcoin was trading at $67.66, at press time, following a hike of just 1% in the last 24 hours. Its price was still a long way from its late-October levels when it briefly climbed above $95. Since then, it’s been mostly downhill for the crypto.

There seemed to be some sign of a breather though. The RSI was below 30 during that drop. It has since come back to just nudging above its average.

The CMF at -0.06 suggested that sellers still had the upper hand, but the outflows were clearly weaker than earlier this month.

Final Summary

  • Hong Kong’s SFC added Hyperliquid to its Alert List for operating without a licence.
  • Long holders on Anthropic perps on Hyperliquid hit a record 5,567.

data.title: Is poor demand the reason behind Roundhill ditching XRP, Solana income ETF plans?
data.description:
On the back of an iffy Q3, many were hoping Q4 would turn out to be better. Unfortunately, that hasn’t been the case. Especially for those in the XRP and Solana markets.

Abandoned without explanation

Both these altcoins are in the news today after Roundhill ETF Trust revealed that it will be ditching plans to launch two exchange-traded funds or ETFs tied to them. It cited no specific reason in its filings with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission for these new plans.

In fact, all it said was,

The Trust no longer intends to seek effectiveness of the Fund.

It went on to add that “… no securities of the Fund were sold, or will be sold.”

The registration documents for both these ETFs were filed way back in October 2025. That’s over a year ago. As recently as 06 November, the Trust had submitted an extension. This would have allowed the registrations to become effective by 06 December.

Little interest in Roundhill’s proposed ETFs?

However, an important distinction must be made here. It must be pointed out that the ETFs Roundhill was planning to launch were income-focused products. These ETFs would have relied on income generated by trading Options linked to existing crypto prodcuts.

Now, while more recent and fewer in number compared to funds that directly hold these tokens, these products have seen little interest lately.

Consider Amplify’s SOLM, for instance. At the time of writing, it held net assets worth just $1.36 million. This, despite being launched in November last year. Similarly, the fund manager’s XRPM had net assets worth just over $7.66 million in over a year since its launch.

How are Spot Solana and XRP ETFs doing?

These numbers are pretty startling, especially when compared to and juxtaposed against the figures reported by other Solana or XRP-focused ETFs. According to SoSoValue, for instance, combined, both these ETF products attracted over $969 million from May to October 2026.

This, despite recent market weakness hitting these ETF products too. Less than 24 hours ago, XRP ETFs saw outflows of over $6 million, with the Canary XRP ETF (XRPC) and the Grayscale XRP Trust ETF (GXRP) particulalry affected. This, after the week ending ending 13th November saw outflows of $19.1 million. This was the largest single-week withdrawal in nearly eight months.

In a similar vein, the assets under management for Spot Solana ETFs fell from $1.79 billion on 25th September to $947 million on 18th November.

Final Summary

  • Roundhill ETF Trust no longer seeks effectiveness of its income-focused XRP, Solana products.
  • Spot ETFs have seen weak inflows lately thanks to the broader market’s bearish trend.

data.title: Bitcoin’s $2.58B ETF outflows deepen November sell-off – Is $60K next?
data.description:
Bitcoin’s [BTC] price slide is accelerating, with the king coin falling below $63,000 amid a new wave of ETF outflows and a broader rotation of capital into the AI sector.

The drop extends a brutal month that has seen roughly $2.58 billion flee U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs since the start of November.

Why are BTC prices falling?

On the 19th of November, Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a net outflow of $306.50 million, with BlackRock’s IBIT accounting for $209.5 million, roughly 87% of the day’s redemptions.

The price action followed the outflows, as Bitcoin traded near $63,071 at the time of writing, down nearly 3% on the day and hovering at its lowest levels since mid-August. Ethereum fared worse, though, dropping below $1,800 at press time.

Another massive factor behind Bitcoin’s fall was noted by the X account Why Markets Move. It stated that currently, investors are seeing more potential in the AI boom and the upcoming Anthropic IPO, compared to crypto.

For the uninitiated, Anthropic is currently targeting a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion in its Nasdaq listing, with investors such as Nvidia and Microsoft. This is undoubtedly good news for AI, but not such much for digital assets.

Macro conditions vs. Bitcoin

Raj Kamal, founder and CEO of TransFi, told AMBCrypto how policy shifts and macro conditions can crush crypto sentiment. He said,

I think the market read the result as a short-term negative for crypto. Much of the rise in bitcoin and in stablecoin adoption came after the 2024 US election, and investors now expect closer scrutiny of consumer protection, anti-money-laundering rules and the crypto interests of President Trump’s family.

Kamal also outlined how ETF redemptions became another salient point for Bitcoin’s fall.

 

U.S. Spot bitcoin ETFs recorded about $1.91 billion of net outflows over seven straight sessions from 5 to 13 November. Institutional money began to leave as the price fell, and once Bitcoin went below $70,000, leveraged positions were flushed out.

His outlook was playing out in real life, with November’s cumulative ETF outflows now exceeding $2.5 billion until press time. The CEO ended with a warning.

I don’t think that flushing out is over yet.

On a similar note, stablecoin supply has plunged by roughly $14.28 billion over the past thirty days, signaling a broader drain of dollar liquidity from the crypto ecosystem.

The AI rotation has to simmer down, and regulatory clarity needs to improve for Bitcoin, otherwise its downward spiral will not stop. Therefore, traders have to now watch the $62,000 support level, but a sustained break below will lead BTC to $60,000.

Final Summary

  • U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $239.9 million in net outflows on November 19, bringing November’s total outflows to almost $2.58 billion.
  • The AI boom, especially Anthropic’s upcoming IPO, is a potential drain for crypto markets.

data.title: Venice Token reclaims $22 as Arthur Hayes eyes a VVV rally toward $40
data.description:
The utility and access token for the generative platform Venice AI, Venice Token [VVV], has rallied 7.22% in the past 24 hours. It has climbed 17.2% over the past week, putting in a strong performance at a time when most of the rest of crypto was facing selling pressure.

Its daily trading volume has also leapt by 54%, to $54.45 million, according to CoinMarketCap data.

VVV to $40 before the AI bubble bursts

In a post on X, crypto exchange BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes wrote that he expected a Venice Token rally. Three other altcoins, namely Ethereum, NEAR, and ZCash, were also mentioned.

He set a price target of $40 for VVV, as well as $2,800 for ETH, $1,800 for ZEC, and $6 for NEAR.

In May, he had grouped ZEC with Hyperliquid and called for a sizeable rally for both tokens. ZEC nearly reached his $1,000 target shortly thereafter.

On the weekly chart, Venice Token presented an attractive buying opportunity. After the strong rally from $9.81 to $34.61 earlier this year, the altcoin saw a correction, reaching as low as $16.73 a week ago.

However, the weekly trading session did not close below $19.28, the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level. The bullish reaction after the sweep of this retracement level suggested bulls were beginning to take control of the market.

There was a long way to go, and the wider market sentiment could affect VVV negatively. Based on the evidence at hand, the defense of the $19.8 demand zone indicated bullishness.

The immediate target is the $34 highs, and $40 might be possible, but the route there is unclear.

Short-term VVV outlook flips bullishly

The 4-hour chart displayed a series of lower highs and lower lows in recent weeks, a downtrend. The latest lower high at $19.72 was flipped to support on Monday.

Furthermore, the altcoin has managed to climb past $22.14 and breached the 50% higher timeframe retracement level, too.

Swing traders and long-term investors can look to buy Venice Token. A breakdown below $20.16 will flip the H4 bias bearish, while a drop below $16.74 will signal a deeper correction on the weekly timeframe.

Final Summary

  • Arthur Hayes called for a VVV rally to $40 before the AI boom unwinds.
  • The altcoin’s weekly chart and the sweep of the $19 demand zone were a bullish sign, and the next target is $34.61.

data.title: Top 9 crypto exchanges of November 2026
data.description:
Cryptocurrency exchanges operate by acting as a connecting platform between buyers and sellers. They provide users with a trading platform to create accounts, complete their KYC, deposit and withdraw funds, and start trading in the supported cryptocurrencies.

Users can access features like spot, futures, and derivatives trading. There are wallets available that allow them to store, deposit, and withdraw digital assets. Crypto exchanges make markets accessible to individuals and institutions around the world and provide liquidity. Here is our list of the top 9 crypto exchanges of November 2026:

1. Binance

Binance was established in 2017 and is one of the biggest crypto exchanges in the world. It has evolved into one of the most comprehensive ecosystems that caters to retail investors, developers, and institutional customers.

It has a lot of trading services, including spot, margin, futures, and peer-to-peer trading in supported markets. There are also advanced charting tools, trading indicators, various order types, and market analysis that support different types of trading.

2. OKX

Founded in 2017, OKX has developed a broader ecosystem over time that includes Web3 services, derivatives, cryptocurrency trading, and blockchain-related products. The platform is a great pick for retail users, and professional traders alike.

It has the options of spot trading, margin trading, futures, and perpetual swaps. There are market charts, technical indicators, order management features and tools that are designed for amateur and experienced traders.

3. Kraken

Kraken was founded in 2011 and is one of the oldest exchanges in the space. It supports cryptocurrency buying, selling, and spot trading while the Kraken Pro platform has advanced trading options that include market charts, order books, technical analysis and different order execution options.

There are margin trading, futures, staking options also available on the platform. They have a strong focus on security which includes measures like encryption, account protection features, two-factor authentication, and secure digital asset custody arrangements.

4. Bitget

Bitget has spot and futures trading along with other digital asset trading options. It has real-time market information, technical charts, trading indicators, and order management features. Copy trading is one of its major distinctive products that lets users replicate trading strategies from other traders on the platform.

There are security measures like withdrawal controls, risk monitoring and asset protection mechanisms in place to ensure user safety. They also support a lot of crypto and trading pairs letting users access to different digital asset markets.

5. KuCoin

KuCoin has a wide range of cryptocurrencies and trading services and provides traders access to digital assets, spot trading, margin trading, and futures. There are trading charts, technical indicators, multiple order types, trading charts and market information.

There are also trading bots available that allow users to automate selected trading strategies. Lending-related products, and wallet integrations are also part of the KuCoin platform.

6. Crypto.com

Crypto.com was established in 2016 and created a broad ecosystem over the years that includes cryptocurrency trading, payments, digital wallets, and other blockchain-related products. It also has a crypto wallet, payment-related products and eligible digital asset earning programmes.

The security measures on Crypto.com include multi-factor authentication, withdrawal protection, digital asset custody controls and account monitoring. The exchange is also known for its customer-oriented approach and efforts to connect crypto services with everyday financial activities.

7. Bitfinex

Bitfinex offers margin trading, spot trading and derivatives products along with lending and funding related services in supported markets. There are detailed order books, customizable trading layouts, advanced charts and multiple order charts.

The advanced trading interface and liquidity infrastructure distinguish it from platforms designed primarily for beginners. In terms of security measures as well, Bitfinex has monitoring mechanisms in place and multi-factor authentication as well.

8. Coinbase

Coinbase started out in 2012 and has developed its services beyond cryptocurrency buying and selling to include institutional custody, and many blockchain-related products that are useful for advanced and beginner users. It was created with the vision of making crypto accessible through a secure and user-friendly digital platform.

The platform has an Advanced trading experience that lets traders use features such as real-time market charts, order books, price indicators, and advanced order execution options. Coinbase Prime gives eligible institutions access to trading, custody, and other digital asset infrastructure.

9. Gate

Gate supports a wide range of digital assets and crypto trading pairs. Its ecosystem has options like spot trading, margin trading, futures trading, digital asset management, Web3 services, and derivatives.

Gate supports 5,400 digital assets and has over 63 million users around the world with lightning-fast listings for new and trending tokens.

Conclusion

Crypto exchanges are an essential part of the global financial system and important towards driving mainstream crypto adoption. Exchanges connect individuals, businesses, institutional investors and financial markets and aren’t just trading platforms but also enablers of digital adoption.

As with any financial decision, users should conduct their own research, review an exchange’s security measures and fee structure, and fully understand the risks involved before committing significant funds.

data.title: Michael Saylor prioritizes STRC buybacks as Strategy’s Bitcoin buying slows 90% – Why?
data.description:
Nothing highlights the impact of ongoing market volatility better than Strategy.

In a recent interview, Michael Saylor outlined a potential shift in Strategy’s approach. He explained why the company could sell MSTR shares even below its net Bitcoin value to buy back STRC. The key takeaway? The market is calling this arguably the most revealing part of the 19th of November’s investor Q&A.

Fundamentally, this seems logical. As outlined below, MSTR has performed extremely poorly as Bitcoin has fallen, losing over 40% of value within Q4. If MSTR loses another 25% of value, it will have lost more this quarter than last year’s Q4 crash, potentially making it the worst quarter MSTR has had since the bear market back in 2022.

The result? Strategy’s Bitcoin [BTC] accumulation has slowed sharply in Q4 2026. 

In Q4 2025, Strategy bought 32,470 BTC. In comparison, it has only bought 3,183 BTC so far in Q4 2026. This represents a drop of 90%. To date, Strategy also used $206.3 million proceeds from selling MSTR shares to buy STRC shares. However, only $33.4 million has been used to buy Bitcoin.

In short, broader market weakness is putting Strategy under pressure. Against this backdrop, Michael Saylor’s latest STRC strategy doesn’t look like a random move. Strategy seems to be shifting more capital toward supporting its preferred stock while navigating a difficult market. But with FUD around the company continuing to build, the bigger question is whether STRC can still attract enough investor demand to support Strategy’s Bitcoin accumulation plans.

STRC buybacks could change Strategy’s Bitcoin playbook

One thing is clear: Strategy’s main priority is to keep STRC stable.

As one analyst pointed out, this could mean the company would continue selling MSTR shares to fund STRC buybacks. If that isn’t enough, Strategy could also sell Bitcoin whenever STRC trades below its $100 par value. Saylor believes STRC’s 12% dividend is already attractive enough, making it a key income-generating product for institutional investors.

But what does this mean for Strategy shareholders? As the chart below shows, major institutional investors increased their MSTR holdings in Q3 2026. The top 15 now own around 33% of all outstanding shares. This shows that big investors are still interested in MSTR despite market weakness.

However, with Strategy focusing more on STRC, will MSTR shareholders still benefit from its BTC strategy?

Notably, this is where a potential feedback loop comes in. Continued weakness in MSTR could push Strategy to rely more on STRC buybacks to support its capital structure. However, this could also put institutional demand for MSTR at risk. If investor confidence weakens, raising fresh capital for future STRC buybacks could become more difficult.

So, for now, Saylor’s shift towards STRC signals a “risky” change in how Strategy plans to fund future BTC purchases.

Final Summary

data.title: Bitcoin institutional holdings hit $29.78B – What changed in Q3?
data.description:
Things have changed dramatically since the third quarter of 2026, when institutional interest in Bitcoin [BTC] increased. After three quarters of net selling, institutional investors resumed net purchases of spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products (ETPs).

According to Alex Thorn from Galaxy Research, institutions added approximately 49,229 BTC-equivalent during the three-month period.  Notably, by the 30th of September, institutional investment managers held a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent, worth approximately $29.78 billion.

How did Q3 2026 flip the script?

The growing role of financial advisors and wealth management platforms played a major role.

Together, they held 144,307 BTC-equivalent by the end of September, representing 40.5% of all Bitcoin ETP holdings reported by institutional managers. If looked back, their holdings have increased for nine consecutive quarters and are now 3.3 times higher than their March 2024 levels.

That being said, large banks played a major role in this accumulation, with Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley being among the biggest buyers during Q3.

Wells Fargo alone added 14,636 BTC-equivalent, taking its total holdings to 30,553 BTC-equivalent, making it the largest institutional holder of U.S. spot Bitcoin ETPs, overtaking Jane Street.

Institutional ownership also shifted, with hedge funds dropping from 50.6% in December 2024 to 19%, while financial advisors and wealth platforms increased their exposure. Of this, BlackRock’s IBIT accounted for 65.2% of institutional Bitcoin ETP holdings.

Bitcoin ETP vs. ETF holdings

That said, Bitcoin ETP holdings fell by 38,531 BTC between the 30th of September and the 16th of November.

However, the tokenized ETP sector continued to struggle, with its market capitalization falling 6.2% to $595 million and trading volume declining to $160 million, as previously reported by AMBCrypto.

This comes as Bitcoin spot ETFs recorded net inflows of $2.65 billion in September 2026 and $3.52 billion in August, while July saw smaller inflows of $172.43 million. However, the trend reversed in October, with $515.03 million in net outflows, followed by significantly larger outflows of $3.47 billion in November 2026.

Final Summary

  • Institutional investment managers held a record 356,491 BTC-equivalent, worth approximately $29.78 billion.
  • Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley were among the biggest buyers during Q3.

data.title: Cardano’s $5M conference budget has a $1M problem — Details!
data.description:
The Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

First it was copper, now it’s conferences

On 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and New York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

So, where does the money go?

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

According to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

However, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

For the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

ADA near $0.155 as traders return

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

Final Summary

  • Cardano Foundation wants the treasury to fund 12 crypto conferences in 2027.
  • Budget assumes ADA at $0.20, but with ADA near $0.155, the request falls over $1 million short.

data.title: ‘Fall now, rally later’ –  Ripple CEO sees crypto rebound after Anthropic IPO
data.description:
On the 19th of November, Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse said in an interview with CNBC that the recent crypto market sell-off is a result of capital rotating into IPOs like Anthropic. However, he does expect the markets to rebound once the listing is complete.

Still on-chain data for XRP suggests that despite on-chain indicators looking bullish, the altcoin is struggling to move beyond the $1 psychological level.

Garlinghouse: Fall now, rally later

Garlinghouse argued that the recent bloodbath across digital assets is less about a fundamental collapse in crypto and more about investors shifting funds to chase the AI boom.

He pointed to a previous sell-off in the market, acknowledging,

We also saw a sell-off very similar when SpaceX went public. What happens is… people are taking liquidity out of a very liquid market in crypto, including Bitcoin and XRP, and moving it into SpaceX. The exact same thing happened coming into the Athropic IPO… What we saw after the SpaceX IPO is a rally in the crypto market.

He believes that the same story will play out with the Anthropic IPO too.

The on-chain reality shows tightening supply

Garlinghouse’s bullish thesis does have a solid footing. Most notably, CryptoQuant’s data shows that the XRP Exchange Reserve on Binance has been declining over the last thirty days.

In late October 2026, Binance held roughly 2.7 billion XRP, but the figure dropped to 2.47 billion XRP as of the 19th of November.

When Exchange Reserve falls, it typically signals that investors are moving coins to self-custody, reducing the immediate supply available for selling.

XRP price prediction: What’s next after a $1 rejection?

Despite the tightening supply on exchanges, XRP’s price action remains volatile. At press time, XRP was trading at $0.9834, down 1.4% in the last 24 hours.

The chart further revealed a market struggling to find firm footing. XRP managed to hold above $1 during November 12-14 before a steep drop dragged it down to the $0.90 region.

The last 24 hours saw the asset sail briefly above $1 but faced an immediate rejection, slumping back into the high $0.90s.

What should you expect now?

As XRP remains in a tug-of-war between falling exchange reserves and repeated price rejections at $1.00, investors are uncertain about its next direction.

If Garlinghouse is correct and digital assets do rally after the Anthropic IPO, the rotation will easily cause prices to soar beyond $1. However, until that macroeconomic shift occurs, XRP holders appear content to move their coins off exchanges and wait out the storm.

Final Summary

  • Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse argues the current crypto sell-off is just a temporary rotation into IPOs like Anthropic and expects a reversal once the listing is over.
  • While XRP’s price struggles, its Binance exchange reserves have dropped from 2.7B to 2.47B over 30 days, signaling that investors are holding rather than selling.

data.title: GRAM crypto tests KEY support – Why a drop below $0.98 matters
data.description:
Gram [GRAM] fell by 5.28% on Wednesday, the 18th of October. On the same day, Bitcoin [BTC] faced a 2.89% slide, while the cumulative altcoin market cap dipped by 1.62%.

Could the token be a buying opportunity after the recent volatility, or should traders maintain their bearish bias?

The bullish GRAM trap explored

The 1-month liquidation heatmap for the altcoin presented an interesting situation for traders. Earlier this month, GRAM had rallied to $1.27 as Telegram founder Pavel Durov called the token “ridiculously undervalued.

This rally left behind magnetic zones to either side of the move. The $1 is a psychologically important level that has technical confluence with the rally’s floor.

The liquidity just under this psychological level was likely to pull prices lower. After a sweep of this magnetic zone, a return to the $1.27-$1.30 range appeared possible.

Yet, the price trend in place for GRAM meant such a swing buy trade might not be feasible.

Ranges and liquidity sweeps for GRAM traders to watch

On the daily timeframe, the rally earlier this month swept the $1.27 high from October. The immediate rejection showed the sellers had the upper hand.

The daily RSI has also remained below neutral 50 for over a month, reinforcing that bearish momentum was prevalent. The $1.00-$1.07 area was a local demand zone to watch, and the OBV’s upcoming trends could give clues on the next price move’s direction.

The 1-hour chart showed a short-term range formation between $1.00 and $1.09, with the mid-range level at $1.045. At the time of writing, the price was within the lower bounds of the range.

As things stand, traders can look to buy at $1. A price drop below $0.978 would be a warning sign that bears were forcing a breakdown, and could invalidate the short-term range-low buying opportunity, which is risky given the higher timeframe trend.

A bounce toward $1.045-$1.09, or a breakdown below $0.98, might offer a more likely trading opportunity for sellers looking to enter.

Final Summary

  • The Gram rally earlier this month after the token was said to be “undervalued” was immediately sold off.
  • The price action showed a short-term range, but the sellers have the advantage, and buying here could be risky.
